body: Shungite is a black rock with a high carbon content. The commercial stone is quarried in Karelia, in north west Russia, and it takes its name from the village of Shunga. That is a fact about the mineral and not about this piece: the listing does not say where this one came out of the ground.
Elite Noble is a trade word for the shiny, high carbon sort. It arrives with no assay, so this page prints no carbon figure of its own.
A weight, about 20 to 30 g, and a price. That is the whole of the specification, and everything else on the sheet below says not printed.
No dimensions, no finish, no origin for this piece, no certificate. If any of that gets printed it goes on the sheet, and until then the rows stay empty.

acc.summary: What this page does not say
body: The listing this stone came from makes a number of statements about what it does. None of them are repeated here, and none of them are made here in different words either.
It is a rock. We sell it as a rock, and there is nothing you have to do with it.
Sent out from 599 Smithdown Road, Liverpool, Tuesday to Sunday. UK delivery is free over £50, or you can collect from the shop between 10 and 6, any day except Monday.

spec.label: Objects · 01
spec.intro: A rock has a short sheet. Everything the listing prints is in the first three rows, and the rest of it is what the listing does not print.
spec.caption: Elite Noble Shungite Stone
rows: Makeup
Shungite, a black rock with a high carbon content. One piece, nothing added.
Weight
About 20 to 30 g, as printed. It is given as a range, so the piece you are sent sits somewhere inside it.
Price
£26.99 for one piece. One size, and the listing offers no variants.
Grade
The listing calls it Elite Noble, the trade word for the shiny, high carbon sort. No assay comes with it, so no carbon percentage is printed on this page.
Dimensions
Not printed. The listing gives a weight and no measurements.
Finish
Not printed. The listing does not say whether the piece is raw, tumbled or polished.
Origin
Not printed for this piece. Shungite as a mineral is quarried in Karelia, north west Russia, which is a statement about the rock rather than about this stone.
Certificate
None supplied. No assay, no laboratory report and no purity certificate, so there is no figure here to quote.
Use
The listing prints a suggested use. It cannot be separated from a claim we are not able to make, so it is not repeated here.
Suitable for
Anybody. It is an object, not something you take.
Not for
It is not a food and it is not a supplement. Do not put it in your mouth, and keep it away from young children, who put small hard things in theirs.

doctrine.h3: We publish the specification. We do not publish claims about what it does.
doctrine.p: The specification of a rock is a weight, a price and the name of the mineral. The listing this stone came from says a great deal beyond that. None of it is on this page, in those words or in any others, because none of it is something we are able to stand behind.

reiss.label: From Reiss
paras: I stock shungite because people come into the shop and ask for it by name. What I will not do is print the reason they ask for it, because the reason is a claim and I cannot stand a claim up with a weight and a price.

So the page tells you what the rock is, what it weighs, what it costs, and where the mineral comes from generally. If you came here to find out what it will do for you, this is not the page that tells you, and I would rather lose the sale than write it.
reiss.pull: I would rather lose the sale than write it.
